title: First-leaf updates gave no clear first-bloom forecast gain in four US shrub samples in 1980-2008
abstract: We tested a first-bloom date update from the first-leaf date of the same shrub. Each test used only earlier paired years for that plant. The baseline was the past mean bloom date, bounded below by current first leaf. Four East and West samples in 1980-2008 used 4,815 pairs. Mean error reductions ranged from -1.45 to 0.54 days. All four adjusted intervals included zero. Update errors ranged from 6.33 to 9.42 days. Missing visits and report times can link recorded dates and reduce useful lead. These are past-only archive tests, not live forecasts or causal climate effects. The package has a fixed data panel, all predictions, source hashes, code, checks and a figure.

display.caption: Past-only first-bloom date errors and paired error reductions. Positive reductions favor the first-leaf update. Bars show intervals adjusted for four tests.

citations.reason: We extend the earlier-stage update idea to first leaf and first bloom. We write new code and build a new panel from the same archive.
Record availability after leaf reports can select the scored sample.
